newsitem.title: USA: Great Western sees Q4 charges of $115 mln.
newsitem.headline: Great Western sees Q4 charges of $115 mln.

text.p: Great Western Financial Corp will cut 800 jobs and take pretax charges totaling an estimated $115 million in the fourth quarter, the Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday.

Trying to shed operating expenses, the giant thrift-holding company based in Chatsworth, Calif., said it would take pretax charges of $65 million to $70 million to reduce its work force by 800 positions, consolidate its chain of mortgage banking branches and other office space, and install new technology, according to the Journal story.

In addition, the story said, it will incur a $50 million to $60 million charge from selling off $300 million of nonperforming assets and a $21 million charge to buy back $280 million of subordinated debt.
The story said these charges will be partially offset by a $23 million gain on the previously announced agreement to sell the thrift's student-lending business.
